newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called little changed, cash holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called little changed, cash holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open little changed Thursday amid talk of steady cash despite a higher-than-expected injection rate, market sources said.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.085 to $2.095 at 0930 EDT after settling Wednesday at $2.098 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, August dipped to a low of $2.085 after AGA reported an injection rate of 96 bcf.
"We are not breaking down. Cash remains at a premium to the board," one trader said, adding he expected an uptick when the heat returns to the East and Midwest.

According to AGA, overall stocks climbed to 222 bcf, or 15 percent, over year-ago. Eastern storage gained 64 bcf and remained 78 bcf, or 10 percent, above last year, while western inventories continued to lag 1996 levels by seven percent. Producing region stocks, which climbed 21 bcf last week, were still 51 percent over year ago.
Chart traders said August support was at $2.05 and $2, while resistance was seen at $2.15 and along the down trendline at $2.25.
In Wednesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed two cents to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were three cents higher in the low-$2s, while New York city gate gas held steady in the high-$2.30s.
Early Thursday, cash prices at Henry Hub were talked at $2.13-2.15.
